What pass requires: The lesson names at least two moments of student-to-student talk, whatever the period's length. Each has a named move, a question worth talking about, a sentence stem for the first speaker, a job for the listener, and says who is Partner A. Fail = fewer than two, or any move missing its question, stem, or listener's job.
Notes: What counts is the move, not the minutes; P-M3 governs the length of a math Discuss block.

Criterion: Blocks sized to the period and the grade
What pass requires: The agenda's minutes sum exactly to the period the teacher gave, transitions inside the blocks. No block runs longer than the grade allows (about 10 minutes in K-2, 15 in grades 3-5, 20 from grade 6 up) without a check-in splitting it. Fail = minutes that don't sum to the period, or an overlong block.

Criterion: One short line per home language
What pass requires: Every question and direction a student acts on, in the packet and on the slides, carries one line in each home language listed for the class, in the listed order. Each line says the task only (stems, hints, examples and headlines stay in the language of instruction) and runs no longer than about a fifth over the English it supports. Fail = a missing line, a translated scaffold, or a line that doesn't say the task.
Notes: The render report and the deck checker count the lines; the judge reads whether they say the task.

What pass requires: No prompt is on a different page from its answer space, in Word or in the Google Doc Drive makes, and the packet fits its page budget (two pages up to an hour, never more than four). Fail = any task split across a page, or a packet over budget.
Notes: Measured by check_packet.py; the judge reads its report.

Criterion: Key words taught where they land
What pass requires: Three to six key words are named for the lesson. Each is defined in the sentence or on the slide where it first appears, marked the first time a packet section uses it (never every time, never in a word bank), and used in at least one student task. Fail = a key word never used, never defined where it lands, or marked everywhere.

The packet holds about one task per seven minutes of the period, every task serving the objective: no copy-the-definition items, no fifth repetition of a skill already shown, no question answered by the text above it. Each composed answer has a stem on its first line; each task has write space sized to the answer. Fail = busywork items, or a packet with more tasks than the period can hold.

Criterion: The talk-through comes before the build
What pass requires: Before rendering anything, the model presents in chat: a point of view naming what is hard about the idea for these students, a how-might-we question, the arc (objective with standard code, agenda with minutes, one line per block, what students write), and two or three genuine choices with a recommendation. It builds only after the teacher says go. Fail = materials rendered before the teacher could steer, or a single option presented as a choice.
Notes: Waived when the teacher asks to skip straight to the build.

What pass requires: The model asks at most one round of at most three questions, and only for what the request, the class profile, and the conversation don't answer: the lesson, the period length when unknown, and learners as one multi-select question when nothing is on file. Fail = a question whose answer was already available, a second round when the first answered the lesson, or a guessed period length.

Criterion: The plan in chat is complete
What pass requires: The chat response carries the whole plan: objective with the standard verbatim once and the prerequisite, agenda summing to the period, the blocks with say-aloud lines and three look-fors for the main work block, the talk moves, media, differentiation (accommodations, language access, one UDL move per principle), at least three predicted errors each with the wrong answer, why, and the move, the answer key, the closing check, and what to keep if time is cut. Fail = any part missing.
Notes: Judge it as the lesson plan (README, grading rules); never fail it for not being a document.

What pass requires: The model uses the class profile, class notes, or previous lesson that was available, without re-asking what they answer, and says in one line which lesson it built from. The do-now reaches back to that lesson when there is one. Fail = re-asking known information, or ignoring an available previous lesson.

The delivering message names the moment the lesson is most likely to fail and the observable that would show it, asks for reaction (I like / I wish / what if or equivalent), and offers three specific next moves drawn from this lesson, the slide deck first when none was built. Fail = no watch-for, or generic next moves.
